# The audits

<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by `python3 audit_registry.py --write` from `audit_registry.py`. Do not edit: change the registry and regenerate. -->

The mod has 52 offline audits. Each reads the mod's files and flags something the engine accepts without a word and then gets wrong in play. 49 run on every `POST /reload` and feed its `warnings` array; 49 run in CI and fail the build.

Run them all, in parallel, the way CI does:

```sh
.venv/bin/python scripts/run_audits.py            # every CI audit
.venv/bin/python scripts/run_audits.py prev_scope  # one or more, by name
```

When one fails, the runner prints what the flag means and the comment that suppresses an intended one. A suppression is a dated, reasoned comment in the mod file; the placement differs by audit because each reads a different line. For the tagged forms, a tag that no longer matches a flag fails `--strict`, so a stale comment can't linger.

One comment on an event's opening line is read by every audit that reads that line. That is why the event audits added later take a tagged comment inside the event instead.

## What each audit catches

| Audit | A flag means | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| `any_limit_audit` | An `any_*` trigger with a `limit = { }` child. `any_*` takes its conditions directly; the engine rejects the block. | CI, reload |
| `iterator_limit_audit` | An iterator whose `limit = { }` is not its first child. The limit filters the whole iteration wherever it sits, so the lines written above it are gated by it too. | CI, reload |
| `delayed_event_trigger_audit` | Not a gate: lists the events queued with a delay whose `trigger` may be false when queued, which seems to drop them (#1596), for the play-test that settles the rule. | reload |
| `random_list_weight_audit` | A `trigger = { }` in a `random_list` branch's weight `modifier`: the engine rejects the token and the tilt is lost. Use `if = { limit = { ... } add = N }`; the `ai_chance` form is valid. | CI |
| `effect_trigger_validity_audit` | An effect or trigger name the engine doesn't know, or a known one in the wrong kind of block (an effect where triggers are read, or the reverse). The engine logs it at load and drops the line. | CI, reload |
| `script_argument_audit` | A scripted effect or trigger call whose arguments are not exactly the `$X$` names its callee's body uses, or an argument whose value is a `{ }` block. | CI, reload |
| `duplicate_key_audit` | A key repeated inside one modifier-family block. With differing values the last one wins and the first is lost (error); identical repeats are warnings and don't fail CI (#191). | CI, reload |
| `modifier_field_audit` | A modifier type name no definition registers: written as a field in a modifier block (the engine drops the line) or read as `modifier:<name>` (it reads nothing). A name that fits a dynamic family, or that `modifiers.log` lists, still needs its own definition in `common/modifier_type_definitions/`. Also a field whose type vanilla registers without a loc key, so its line shows the raw key. | CI, reload |
| `mod_structure_audit` | Unbalanced braces in a `common/` file (the engine drops the rest of the file), an `INJECT:` on an entity the mod itself defines or REPLACEs (it never applies), and two bare declarations of one top-level name (only one survives). | reload |
| `load_order_audit` | A key whose value in ModState differs from what the engine loads: a bare copy the engine drops for an earlier one (the first bare definition wins, and vanilla's and the mod's files sort together), an `INJECT:` lost to a `REPLACE:` of its key, or a directive on a key nothing defines. Every tool built on ModState then reads a definition the game doesn't use. | CI, reload |
| `attitude_key_audit` | An `attitude = <key>` that is not one of the engine's fifteen attitude keys. | CI, reload |
| `prev_scope_audit` | A `prev` that can only mean a scope the script already names. `prev` is one scope change back, and re-entering `root` in a loop makes it `root`. | CI, reload |
| `empty_effect_audit` | An empty effect block, or an event option with no effect at all. | CI, reload |
| `modifier_multiplier_var_audit` | An `add_modifier { multiplier = var:X }` whose variable can read as `none`: the multiplier resolves against ROOT, not the scope the effect runs in. | CI, reload |
| `je_multiplier_scope_audit` | A country-only read inside a `je:` modifier multiplier, followed through named script values and scripted triggers. Reads through `owner` or an explicit scope path are safe. | CI, reload |
| `modifier_duration_audit` | An `add_modifier` duration written as `{ value = N }` or computed, which the engine reads as 0 days. Followed through helpers' `$DAYS$`. | CI, reload |
| `modifier_visibility_audit` | A modifier value too small to show at its type's `decimals = N`, so the tooltip prints 0. | reload |
| `sol_fraction_audit` | A `*_standard_of_living_add` that is not a whole number and is not scaled before it applies. Standard of living is an integer, so the fraction does nothing on its own (#338). | CI, reload |
| `change_variable_clamp_audit` | A `min =` / `max =` inside `change_variable`, where which way it clamps is a guess. | CI, reload |
| `building_scope_variable_audit` | A variable set or read in building scope. Buildings hold no variables (#519). | CI, reload |
| `variable_guard_audit` | A `has_variable = X` guard (or the global or local form) as a direct child of a `NOT`, `NAND` or `NOR` that also reads `var:X` bare. A multi-child `NOT` reads every child, so the guard protects nothing and an unset X logs `Failed to fetch variable`; read as NOR the block is also wrong when X is set. Move the guard into a limit and keep the rest of the block inside the negation, `trigger_if = { limit = { has_variable = X } NOT = { … } }`; an equality with a number can instead be read as `var:X ?= N`. | CI, reload |
| `container_timed_variable_audit` | A timed variable set on a script container, where it never expires. | CI, reload |
| `je_immediate_reset_audit` | An unguarded write in a journal entry's `immediate`. A revolution's winner re-runs `immediate`, so the write resets state the nation should keep. | CI, reload |
| `orphaned_event_audit` | An event nothing fires (#147). | CI, reload |
| `event_image_audit` | A visible event with no `event_image`. It draws a magenta blob and the engine logs nothing (#353). | CI, reload |
| `event_context_audit` | An event whose text doesn't fit where it fires: a system's event not gated on its game rule, text that says the country did something it never chose, or a foreign action imputed to it. | CI, reload |
| `trigger_event_cycle_audit` | A `trigger_event` with no delay on a cycle of scripted effect calls and other undelayed `trigger_event`s. It runs inside the effect that fires it, so a cycle nothing stops overflows the stack: a crash with no log line. Write what the cycle re-reads before the `trigger_event`, or give it `days = 1`; the comment is for a cycle a write already stops, and names that write. | CI, reload |
| `tooltip_walk_variable_audit` | A variable read after a `set_variable` of it in one body a tooltip walks (a scripted GUI's or a button's `effect`, an event option, a decision's `when_taken`). The walk writes nothing, so the read finds it unset and logs every frame the tooltip shows. Compare the values directly, guard the read with `has_variable`, use `?=`, or put the body behind a click-only marker; names other code keeps set are left out. | CI |
| `faith_scene_audit` | An event text with one faith's word in it (a priest, a mosque, a guru, the faith's name) that a country of another state religion can be shown: its title, description, flavor, option, tooltip or a modifier it adds. Write the scene without a named faith, or gate that version on the faith (#1531). | CI, reload |
| `silent_variable_audit` | An event option that moves a number the UI shows with `change_variable` / `set_variable`, which render nothing in the tooltip. Wrap it in a `custom_tooltip`. | CI, reload |
| `kill_character_audit` | A `kill_character` in an event with no guard that the character exists. | CI, reload |
| `event_magnitude_audit` | A hardcoded amount in an event for a resource that grows fast over the game (prestige is the model case), which is invisible at late-game scale. | CI, reload |
| `treaty_leverage_side_audit` | A treaty article with `country_treaty_leverage_generation_add` on the side that pays, or one that builds no Involvement because it lacks `max_target_involvement` / `target_involvement_applies_to` or names the wrong side; and a diplomatic action's pact that builds none or departs from vanilla's pact convention (`source_country`, or `mutual`). | CI, reload |
| `treaty_evaluation_scope_audit` | A named-scope read in a treaty article's AI `evaluation_chance`, which sees only root; or a party scope in a block that does not bind it: `scope:source_country` / `scope:target_country` in `visible` / `possible` (use root and `scope:other_country`), or `scope:other_country` in `can_ratify` / `requirement_to_maintain` / `can_propose` (use source / target; first / second on a mutual article). | CI |
| `principle_tier_audit` | A power bloc principle tier that drops a modifier the tier below carried. Tiers replace each other, so each restates everything below it. | CI, reload |
| `prestige_good_roster_audit` | A company prestige good no `building_types` building of the company can make, one on a `local = yes` good, or a fourth prestige good on one base good (the engine keeps three). | CI, reload |
| `amendment_reachability_audit` | An amendment no script attaches, or an `add_amendment` whose type names no amendment. | CI, reload |
| `ideology_lawgroup_audit` | An ideology's lawgroup block that leaves out a law of its group, which makes the ideology neutral on it. | CI, reload |
| `roster_membership_audit` | A mod ship type with no `ai_ship_category` (required since vanilla 1.14.4), an unknown one, or no fleet entity row; a ship modification no ship type lists in a slot, so it can never be fitted; or a production method no production method group lists. | CI, reload |
| `pm_employment_audit` | A building where some valid production-method combination drives a profession's employment below zero. | CI, reload |
| `loc_coverage_audit` | A mod entity (modifier, journal entry, button, building, method...) with no loc key. The game shows the raw key and logs nothing. | CI, reload |
| `script_loc_reference_audit` | A loc key named in script (`desc = "KEY"`, `text = KEY`) that no loc file defines. | CI, reload |
| `loc_render_audit` | Bracket-style formatting in a loc value (`[b]x[/b]`), which errors on every render: write `#b x#!`. Also a formatting tag left open at the end of a value (`#bold` with no `#!`), which runs on into the text after it, and a `#` that is no tag: write a literal hash as `##`. | CI, reload |
| `loc_script_value_audit` | A `ScriptValue('x')` in loc or a script string that names no script value. It renders 0. | CI, reload |
| `loc_root_context_audit` | A loc key on a country root that doesn't fit where it renders, reached there by a `$KEY$` splice, a named key or a `GetCustom` entry. A `ROOT.`, `SCOPE.` or `THIS.` read in a key a widget renders comes out blank. A `JournalEntry.` or `Country.` read in a `status_desc` key or a scripted button's text is the unproven root there (not known to fail): use the proven one, `ROOT.GetCountry…`. An entry or player read on a public tab shows another country the player's figure, or nothing. | CI, reload |
| `concept_reference_audit` | A loc link to a game concept that doesn't exist. The link breaks and logs three errors a render (#1257). | CI, reload |
| `localization_accessor_audit` | A loc accessor chain (`[X.Y.Z]`) the engine's data-type catalog doesn't allow. The engine renders it as nothing. | CI, reload |
| `gui_reference_audit` | A mod `.gui` or journal-entry widget mount that names a loc key, scripted GUI, script value, type or concept that doesn't exist. | CI, reload |
| `texture_reference_audit` | An asset path in script that names no file, or an entity that declares no art field its type needs. The engine logs a missing texture only on first render. | CI, reload |
| `long_tooltip_audit` | Live GUI text or a tooltip over 500 rendered characters outside a How section. The rules belong in How, or in a concept the tooltip links. | CI, reload |
| `hidden_modifier_audit` | A `custom_tooltip` around an `add_modifier` whose text renders no `GetStaticModifier` for it: the player sees the text and none of the modifier's lines. | CI, reload |
| `button_reason_audit` | A button a scripted GUI greys out whose tooltip doesn't say why, or one whose reason prints as raw script. | CI, reload |

| `iterator_limit_audit` | `# REVIEWED YYYY-MM-DD: why` | trailing on the `limit = {` line or the iterator's opener line |
| `delayed_event_trigger_audit` | `# REVIEWED YYYY-MM-DD: why` | trailing on the target event's `trigger = {` line |
| `random_list_weight_audit` | none | Fix the flag. |

| `script_argument_audit` | `# REVIEWED YYYY-MM-DD (script_argument): why` | on the call's line (its opening line for a multi-line call) |
| `duplicate_key_audit` | `# REVIEWED YYYY-MM-DD: why` | trailing on the duplicate's line |
| `modifier_field_audit` | `# REVIEWED YYYY-MM-DD (modifier_field_loc): why` | for a missing loc key only, trailing on a modifier block's line that writes the field (one comment covers every use); an unregistered name takes none |
| `mod_structure_audit` | `# REVIEWED YYYY-MM-DD: why` | trailing on the `INJECT:<name>` line (brace and collision flags take none) |

## Adding an audit

1. Write `<name>_audit.py` at the repo root, and `test_<name>_audit.py` beside it. The audit is the function that finds flags; `audit_common.py` gives it the rest: `parse_reviewed(comment, tags)` reads the `# REVIEWED` comment, `Flag` and `AuditResult` hold the findings (`unreviewed`, `exemptions`, `stale`), `write_report` writes the report with this page's suppression text, and `cli_main(audit_fn)` gives the `--strict` mode that exits 1 on an unreviewed flag or a stale tag. A reload audit also needs `regenerate(mod_state)` returning a dict whose `unreviewed` count feeds the `warnings` array (`audit_common.summary` builds it).
2. Add it to `POST_LOAD_AUDITS` in `mod_state_server.py` if a reload should run it.
3. Add one `Audit(...)` entry to `audit_registry.py`, with `builds_mod_state=True` if its command line builds a `ModState`.
4. Run `python3 audit_registry.py --write` and commit this file with the rest. It also corrects the audit counts `docs/guides/python_tools.md` spells out, and prints what is left there for you to write: a CI audit's row in the command table, its row in the reload table, its name where a sentence lists audits by where they run.

CI, `scripts/preflight.py` and this page all read the registry, `test_audit_registry.py` fails on an audit file the registry leaves out, and `audit_registry.py --check` fails on a count in `python_tools.md` that disagrees with it.
